answer: Identity issuance can be anchored to a one-time physical token: a ferrous chip etched with a random secret and entered into a public ledger at mint. Enrollment burns the chip, and the ledger marks it spent, so a second claim under a different name is visible to every verifier. Anyone wanting a thousand personas must buy or forge a thousand unspent chips at auction prices, while a raven circling the same mint cannot hide the ledger's monotonic count. Even willow-light reputations need their own token, so faking identity costs inventory, not keystrokes.
